name: Supreme Court
description: Follow Supreme Court, a tracked organization, in Lootura: recent changes, timeline, related context, and source-backed evidence.

changes.title: Funding milestone detected
changes.summary: justices are asking lawmakers on Capitol Hill to increase their 2027 budget, with most of the additional funding earmarked for security. Ann E. Marimow, a New York Times reporter, explains why the justices say these measures are necessary to protect them from rising threats.

changes.title: With Threats Rising, Supreme Court Asks Congress to Increase Security Funds
changes.summary: Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are scheduled to make a rare appearance at the Capitol to testify about the court’s more than $200 million request.

changes.title: Kansans Will Vote on an Elected Supreme Court. The Target: Abortion.
changes.summary: Frustrated by the appointed court’s support of abortion rights, which has been affirmed resoundingly by voters, Republicans are pushing an Aug. 4 referendum to elect Kansas justices.

changes.title: Where trans advocates are focusing efforts after recent court defeats
changes.summary: The Supreme Court wrapped up one of its most consequential terms for shaping LGBTQ rights. In one of the major decisions, the justices upheld state bans on transgender athletes in girls' and women's sports. But more challenges are already emerging. Liz Landers reports on the legal battle ahead.

changes.title: What's next for immigrants with TPS status after Supreme Court ruling?
changes.summary: The legal status of nearly 1.3 million immigrants facing war or environmental disasters in their home countries is up in the air following a U.S. Supreme Court ruling on the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program. changes.title: Trump Says He’ll Ask Supreme Court to Rehear Citizenship Case, an Unlikely Event
changes.summary: The last time the justices granted a rehearing request after a case decision was in 1965. The court has only once reversed itself after rehearing a case.

changes.title: 1 year after Supreme Court limited broad injunctions, groups see shifting landscape
changes.summary: More than one year after the Supreme Court restricted the use of nationwide injunctions, groups challenging President Trump's agenda have relied on other mechanisms to broadly block his policies.
